definitions: A vast, flat, treeless Arctic region of Europe, Asia, and North America in which the subsoil is permanently frozen.
A similar region in other parts of the world where the growth of trees is prevented by low temperatures and short growing seasons.
examples: The Alaskan tundra is home to caribou.
Permafrost underlies much of the tundra.
Lichens thrive in the harsh tundra environment.
